title: Shift-clicking or dragging a tier token (or a quest item such as Magtheridon's Head) into My BiS saves the token as the pick, and that pick never counts as obtained
evidence: Failing test: tests/boot-ui/test_mybis.py::tier_token_link_in_picker_does_not_become_a_stuck_pick. Steps: a Paladin opens the Head picker and shift-clicks the link for Helm of the Fallen Champion (29760). The slot is saved as 29760. The Paladin then equips the class tier helm Justicar Diadem (29061) and the bag/equip scan runs. Result: AssertionError: token 29760 stored as the head pick; after equipping the Paladin tier helm 29061 it is still not obtained (card: 'P1  ·  0 / 17 obtained'). The tile keeps showing the token as needed. Cause: ItemDB:GetEquipLoc (Core/ItemDB.lua:309-323) resolves a token to the equip slot of its first piece, so the ItemFits check in BiS:SetSlot (Core/BiS.lua:265) accepts the token. Both the Picker's ChatFrameUtil.InsertLink hook (UI/Picker.lua:116-135) and the drag-drop path (UI/MyBiS.lua:194) call SetSlot. BiS:GetObtainedState (Core/BiS.lua:593-602) only reports a token as obtained while the player holds the token itself. The token pick is then synced as a wanted item, so the council roster Need column, the Items view and the drop-panel candidates keep listing this player for that token after they already equipped the piece.
rootCause: Tokens are treated as equippable in the slot fit check (the first piece's equip location). Nothing on the SetSlot, Picker or drop paths turns a token into the class's piece or refuses it. The obtained logic has no reverse mapping from a token pick to the pieces it can be exchanged for.
proposedFix: Pick one of two fixes. (a) In BiS:SetSlot, refuse tokens: if ns.ItemDB:IsToken(itemID), print "Choose your class's tier piece instead (the picker lists them under the boss)" and return false. Alternatively resolve the token to the single class piece that fits the slot when there is exactly one (Paladins have 3 per token, so usually refuse). (b) In GetObtainedState, treat a token pick as obtained when the player has equipped, carries or banks any piece of ExpandDrop(token) whose TierPieceClass is the player's class. Option (a) is simpler and keeps council data clean.

title: 'Request sync' buttons (Council footer and Settings > About) print 'Sync requested.' even when nothing was sent
evidence: Failing tests: tests/boot-ui/test_council_ui.py::request_sync_buttons_do_not_claim_success_when_rate_limited. Result: AssertionError: council footer: nothing was sent (rate limited) but chat says ['|cffff8000CDLoot|r: Sync requested.'] | settings: nothing was sent (rate limited) but chat says ['|cffff8000CDLoot|r: Sync requested.']. This happens when clicking within 30 s after the automatic login HELLO. Also tests/boot-ui/test_settings.py::settings_request_sync_when_not_in_guild_does_not_claim_success. Result: AssertionError: guildless player told ['|cffff8000CDLoot|r: Sync requested.']. UI/Council.lua:1668-1670 and UI/Settings.lua:438-440 call ns.Sync:SendHello() and print unconditionally. SendHello returns false when rate-limited, not in a guild or the roster is not ready. /cdl sync (Core/Sync.lua:663-666) handles this correctly and prints 'please wait' or 'not in a guild'. The council button also disables itself for 30 s even when nothing was sent.
rootCause: Both buttons ignore Sync:SendHello()'s return value instead of reusing the /cdl sync feedback logic.
proposedFix: Reuse the SlashSync logic, for example by exposing Sync:RequestSync() that returns ok plus a reason and prints the matching message. Or at least do: `if ns.Sync:SendHello() then ns:Print("Sync requested.") else ns:Print("A sync was requested less than 30 seconds ago; please wait.") end`, with a 'not in a guild' or 'waiting for the roster' branch. Disable the council button only when a HELLO was actually sent.

title: Council Items view stays on the previous phase's boss after changing the Phase dropdown
evidence: Failing test: tests/boot-ui/test_council_ui.py::items_view_follows_the_phase_dropdown. Steps: in the demo council's Items view, 'Attumen the Huntsman · Karazhan' (P1) is selected by default; then P3 is chosen in the Phase dropdown. Result: AssertionError: after switching to P3 the Items view still shows 'Attumen the Huntsman · Karazhan  -  12 items · 6 claims' (['Karazhan:Attumen', 1, 6]). The tree now lists Mount Hyjal first, but the P1 boss stays selected and its item list stays shown. The phase onSelect (UI/Council.lua:1601-1604) only sets state.phase. buildTree keeps the old node in any phase (line 449: `key == state.selectedNode`), so nodeExists() is true and the default-selection code in refreshItems (line 1222) never runs.
rootCause: The selected boss node is session state that survives a phase change, and buildTree deliberately keeps the selected node in the tree.
proposedFix: In the phase dropdown's onSelect, set `state.selectedNode = nil; state.focus = nil` before CouncilUI:Refresh(true). The existing default then selects the new phase's first boss with demand. Keep the sticky behaviour only for ShowItem/ShowBoss jumps.

title: After demo mode is turned off, the Council Member view keeps showing a fake demo member
evidence: Failing test: tests/boot-ui/test_demo.py::demo_off_does_not_leave_fake_member_in_council_views. Steps: a real council member (rank 1) turns demo on, opens the Member view for 'Aldrin' (a demo name), then runs /cdl demo off. The Council tab stays open because the player is really on the council. Result: AssertionError: member view still shows demo member 'Aldrin' (pos '- / 1'). The header reads 'Offline · no list received · CDLoot version unknown'. Refresh only fills state.memberKey when it is nil (line 1769). refreshMember (lines 1485-1542) renders whatever key is stored, even when that key is no longer in `order` or in Store:GetAllKeys().
rootCause: Council view state (memberKey, and also selectedNode/focus) is not revalidated on DEMO_TOGGLED / LISTS_RESET.
proposedFix: In CouncilUI:Refresh, reset state.memberKey to order[1] when the view is 'member' and memberKey is not in `order` (or not in Store:GetAllKeys()). Alternatively register a DEMO_TOGGLED handler that clears state.memberKey, state.selectedNode and state.focus before RequestRefresh.

title: A second /reload within 20s of the previous HELLO leaves the client with no council peers for that session (raider edits aren't pushed, council awards aren't sent)
evidence: Failing cases: test_sync_flows.py::j_quick_double_reload_raider_still_shares -> 'edit after a quick double /reload never reached the online council (R's council peers [], status 'Not shared yet — no council member online')'. test_ledger_sync.py::g_quick_double_reload_council_awards_still_reach_peer -> 'award recorded by C2 after a quick double /reload did not reach online council member C1 (C2's council peers: [])'. In both cases the second session's HELLO came 17.1–17.2s after the first. Addon log: H 39.2 -> S 40.95 (reply), H 51.5 -> no S. OnHello replies S only if RateLimit("Hs:"..sender, REPLY_RATE=20) passes (Sync.lua:499), and the council↔council M only if RateLimit("Hm:"..sender, 20) passes (Sync.lua:511). The rate limit is kept on the answering side and keyed by name only. sessionSeen (Sync.lua:31) is emptied on every /reload of the asking client. GetOnlineCouncilPeers (Sync.lua:184-196) needs sessionSeen, and so do MYLIST_COMMITTED pushes (Sync.lua:611-617) and Comm:SendToCouncil for A (Comm.lua:131-153, Ledger.lua:154-163). Result: the whole session shows 'Not shared yet — no council member online'. Nothing reaches the council until the next login or a manual /cdl sync. For a council member, the 10-min periodic manifest exchange only repairs this if a peer happens to pick it.
rootCause: The per-sender reply rate limit (meant to damp repeated HELLOs) sits on the council side and ignores sessions. The asking client loses the council's earlier reply (sessionSeen) at every /reload, but the council still suppresses its answer to the new session's HELLO.
proposedFix: Put a random session nonce in H (e.g. msg.n) and key the S/M reply rate limits on sender..nonce ("Hs:"..sender..":"..n). Alternative: always answer S (a 12-byte whisper) and rate-limit only M. Either way, a new session always gets its S/M.

title: Demo mode leaks fake member names into RAID chat through the drop panel 'Announce' and the council overview 'Announce to raid'
evidence: Failing cases: test_demo_isolation.py::i_real_drop_announce_in_demo_mode_does_not_post_fake_names. In a real ML raid with demo on, a real boss loot window, then DropPanel:AnnounceItem (the per-item Announce button), SendChatMessage RAID gets 'CDLoot: [Teeth of Gruul] - BiS: Aldrin; Alt: Isolde'. test_demo_isolation.py::i_council_overview_announce_in_demo_mode_does_not_post_fake_names: council items view, right-click on the item row, 'Announce to raid' posts 'CDLoot: [Teeth of Gruul] - BiS: Aldrin · Alt: Isolde' to RAID. DropPanel:AnnounceItem (UI/DropPanel.lua:1729-1743) keeps only simulated (drop.test) drops local. BuildAnnounceLine (1707-1726) takes Store:GetWanters (demo records while demo is on, Store.lua:142-148) filtered by Util.IsInMyGroup (the demo raid, Util.lua:490-496). UI/Council.lua announceItem (1041-1066, menu entry at 1075) calls ns.UI:AnnounceLine with no demo check. Roll.lua already does this right: Announce(body, true, '(demo: only shown to you)') at Roll.lua:523/1080. Addendum A §20 requires that no demo data leaks into comms.
rootCause: Neither announce path checks ns.Demo:IsEnabled(); only the Roll module routes demo announcements to local output.
proposedFix: In DropPanel:AnnounceItem/AnnounceAll and Council.lua announceItem: if ns.Demo:IsEnabled(), ns:Print('[demo, not sent] '..line) instead of ns.UI:AnnounceLine (same as test drops). A central guard in UI:AnnounceLine would also work, but Roll deliberately uses its own local path, so a per-caller check is clearer.

title: Award ledger is account-wide and not scoped to a guild: an alt that is council in another guild syncs guild A's loot history to guild B (and back)
evidence: Failing case: test_ledger_sync.py::g_alt_in_other_guild_does_not_leak_ledger -> "guild A's award m1790000030Mainofficer28477 (winner Raidera-Thunderstrike, not in guild B) was synced to guild B's council via the alt's account-wide ledger". CDLootDB is account-wide (TOC '## SavedVariables: CDLootDB'). ns.db.ledger holds every entry with no guild field (Ledger.lua:42-47). Ledger:GetDigest (455-479) digests all entries, and FlushLedgerWant (506-525) serves all of them to any council peer of the current guild. The view (BuildView 219-290) also shows the other guild's awards. By contrast, Store records carry g = guild name (Store.lua:204), and PruneFormerMembers only touches this guild's copies. An officer whose alt is GM or officer in a second guild that uses CDLoot copies each guild's award log into the other. Neither side can remove the entries afterwards.
rootCause: Ledger entries and the digest/LW/LG sync are not scoped to the guild the client is currently in, although the SavedVariables are shared by every character on the account.
proposedFix: Store the guild key (Guild:GetGuildName()..'-'..realm, as in Guild.lua's GuildKey) in each entry, or keep ns.db.ledger[guildKey][id]. Restrict GetDigest, FlushLedgerWant, BuildView, HasAward and CountSince to the current guild's entries. Merge received entries into the receiver's current guild bucket. Migration: assign existing entries to the guild of the first council login.

title: Own 'Shared with council' marker is deleted at every login (peers prune drops ns.db.peers[me], which has no lastSeen)
evidence: Failing case: test_sync_flows.py::j_shared_status_survives_reload -> "own shared marker was dropped at login (ns.db.peers[me] = None), status now 'Not shared yet — no council member online'". Before the /reload: ns.db.peers[me] = {v, sharedRev=1, sharedTs}. MarkShared (Sync.lua:171-182) writes peersDB[me] without lastSeen. Sync:OnInit (Sync.lua:697-701) deletes every entry with (lastSeen or 0) < now - 90 days, so it deletes this one. Sync:OnLogin (742-746) then has nothing to restore. After each login or /reload, a raider whose list is safely shared sees 'Not shared yet — no council member online' (or 'Sharing with council…') until a HELLO/STATE round trip. If no council member is online, it shows that for the whole session.
rootCause: MarkShared doesn't set lastSeen on the own peers entry, and the 90-day peer prune treats a missing lastSeen as 0.
proposedFix: Set p.lastSeen = GetServerTime() in MarkShared, or skip Util.PlayerKey() / entries with sharedRev in the OnInit prune (the player key is known at OnLogin, so the prune could move there).

title: A council member promoted within 30s of its login HELLO gets no data for about 10 minutes (the promotion HELLO is rate-limited and never retried)
evidence: Failing case: test_council_membership.py::e_promoted_right_after_login_hello -> 'promoted council member got no lists for 120+ s (its promotion HELLO was rate limited)'. HELLOs from R2 at [58.0] only. A longer probe (900s timeout) showed that the list only arrived after 550s, through C1's periodic 10-min manifest exchange (601.0 M, 602.0 W, 603.0 R). OnConfigUpdated (Sync.lua:630-639) sends the promotion HELLO via Util.RandomDelay(3, 8, SendHello). SendHello returns false when RateLimit('hello', HELLO_RATE=30) was used by the automatic login HELLO less than 30s earlier (Sync.lua:268). Nothing reschedules it. Raiders don't push to the new member (they push on commit or on H/S/M from it), and it doesn't pull from the other council members.
rootCause: The rate-limit refusal is silent, and the one-shot promotion HELLO has no retry.
proposedFix: In OnConfigUpdated, bypass the HELLO rate limit for the promotion HELLO (e.g. Sync:SendHello(true) with force), or reschedule it with Util.After(HELLO_RATE - elapsed + 1) when SendHello returns false.

title: Decompression bomb: MAX_INFLATED_LEN is checked only after LibDeflate has inflated the whole payload; one 20 KB GUILD message costs every online member about 0.4s
evidence: Failing case: test_sync_hostile.py::f_decompression_bomb_is_cheap_to_reject. A non-council guild member sends one GUILD message: 19,958 wire bytes, level 9 compression, 8 MB inflated. The delivering tick took 1.62s for 4 receivers, about 0.41s of Lua time each. The message is rejected ('payload too large', stats.dropped) but only after the work is done. Decode (Comm.lua:57-66) calls LibDeflate:DecompressDeflate (line 60) and only then checks #inflated > MAX_INFLATED_LEN (line 62). MAX_WIRE_LEN = 24000 (line 24) is about 10x the largest legitimate message: a relay of 8 distinct full lists (5 phases x 17 slots main+alt) is 2,193 bytes, and the largest message in the 40-member run was 338 bytes. Nothing is accepted and no Lua errors occur, so the effect is a repeated hitch for the whole guild. The sender gate before decoding limits this to guild members.
rootCause: The inflate size can't be bounded with LibDeflate, and the wire-size cap is far above what legitimate messages need.
proposedFix: Lower MAX_WIRE_LEN to about 6–8 KB (and cap GUILD-channel messages, which only carry H, lower still). After a sender's message exceeds MAX_INFLATED_LEN, ignore that sender for the rest of the session so a bomb costs at most once.

title: Protocol-mismatch notice can be spammed: alternating first bytes print one chat line per message on every guild member
evidence: Failing case: test_sync_hostile.py::f_alternating_protocol_majors_do_not_flood_chat -> '10 GUILD messages with alternating majors printed 10 chat lines on every member'. An honest client with a constant major prints exactly once (f_wrong_protocol_major_noted_once_and_ignored passes). NotePeerProtocol only compares with the last major remembered for that sender (`if incompatible[key] == major then return end`, Sync.lua:253), so alternating '2'/'3' reprints every time. The sender only needs to be a guild member (Comm dispatch notes the major before decoding). The major byte is also printed raw: a '\255' major showed as 'protocol \xff'.
rootCause: The 'print once' state is keyed by the last major, not by sender.
proposedFix: Keep a notified[key] = true set and print at most once per sender per session. Still record the latest major for the version list.

title: A single STATE r=1e9 from a council member makes the owner's list unshareable and a later auto-restore overwrites newer local data (Sync MAX_REV 1e9 vs Store 2^31-1)
evidence: Failing case: test_sync_hostile.py::f_council_state_with_huge_rev_does_not_brick_the_list -> "the owner's new edit (own rev 1000000001) never reached C1 (C1 holds rev 1); after a /reload the owner's newer local list (hash b96919a2) was replaced by the council's old copy (rev 1, hash 4fd815ca)". OnState -> CheckOwnAgainst -> OnCouncilHasNewer calls BiS:NoteSeenRev(1e9) (BiS.lua:686-691, no upper bound). BiS:Commit then makes rev = max(rev, highestSeenRev)+1 = 1e9+1 (BiS.lua:651). Sync's IsRev caps at MAX_REV = 1e9 (Sync.lua:22, 50-52), so OwnRev() returns 0 (73-76) and OwnEntry refuses to send (125). At the next login H carries r=0, and the council's S{r=1} triggers the automatic restore for rev 0 (Sync.lua:394). AdoptRestored then replaces the newer local list. Store accepts revs up to 2147483647 (Store.lua:19). Only a buggy or hostile council member can send this.
rootCause: The rev limits are inconsistent between Store, Sync and BiS, and an out-of-range own rev is treated as 'no list' (rev 0), which enables automatic restore.
proposedFix: Use one MAX_REV everywhere. Ignore (don't NoteSeenRev) incoming revs that exceed the own rev by an implausible margin (e.g. > rev + 1000). In OwnRev, never map a real own rev to 0; clamp instead, and never auto-restore over a record with picks and a rev > 0.

title: Two council copies of the same rev with different data are never reconciled (manifest and STATE carry revs only)
evidence: Failing case: test_sync_flows.py::c3_same_rev_divergence_is_repaired -> 'council copies of the same rev 2 differ and are never repaired: C1 4fa315c8 (PC A data), C2 b96919a2, owner b96919a2'. Setup: PC A pushes rev 2 (X) to C1 while C2 is away. PC B, with rev-1 SavedVariables, makes a different edit while only C2 is online, which also becomes rev 2 (Y). Afterwards the owner, C1 and C2 are all online together, and nothing changes. GetManifest (Store.lua:221-236) and S (Sync.lua:499-504) carry revs only. PullFrom pulls only rev > have (Sync.lua:322). CheckOwnAgainst on equal revs just marks the list shared (Sync.lua:415-425). The Store:Put rule that accepts an equal rev with a different hash from a direct push (Store.lua:198) is never used, because the owner never pushes on an equal rev. C1 shows stale data until the owner's next edit.
rootCause: Revs alone don't identify a list version when an owner plays on two machines with different SavedVariables.
proposedFix: Add the hash to S (S{r, h}) and to manifest entries (e.g. 'rev:hash8'). The owner pushes when revs are equal and hashes differ (the direct-push rule already accepts it), and PullFrom requests when hashes differ at equal rev. Alternatively, let the owner bump its rev when a council member reports an equal rev with a different hash.

title: Every changed list is sent twice to a returning council member (owner push races the relay pulled from another council member)
evidence: test_sync_traffic.py::h_forty_member_guild_login_waves (passes; the test allows up to 2 copies), note: 'wave 3: 24 of 24 list transfers arrived twice (owner push + council relay race)'. Wave 3 traffic: L=24, R=4 (6 parts) for 12 changed lists x 2 returning council members. On the returning member's HELLO, owners push after RandomDelay(2,10) (Sync.lua:417). Online council members send M after RandomDelay(1,5) (Sync.lua:513-517), and the returning member then pulls the same lists with W and gets R relays. Neither side knows about the other. Related numbers from the same run: an in-sync 40-login wave still costs 208 messages (40 H, 12 M, 156 S). Each council member sends 39–43 CDLc messages, which the per-prefix server throttle spreads over about 44s (231 throttled sends requeued by ChatThrottleLib), so other ctrl messages such as A awards queue behind them.
rootCause: By spec (§10.3), H triggers both owner pushes and council manifest pulls without any coordination.
proposedFix: Optional optimisation: owners skip the delayed push when an online council member already holds their current rev (the returning member will pull it), or the returning member delays its W until owner pushes had a chance (e.g. only request keys whose owner is offline first). Council members could also skip S when cached rev == msg.r == 0.

title: A starter who /reloads and restarts the same roll gets the new roll cancelled on every other client; the award is then ignored raid-wide
evidence: test_rolls.py::starter_reload_then_restarts_same_roll FAILS: "clients run different rolls after the restart: {'Alice': 'Alice-1790000063-1', 'Bob': 'Alice-1790000055-1', 'Carol': 'Alice-1790000055-1', ...} (old Alice-1790000055-1, new Alice-1790000063-1)". Steps: Alice (the ML) starts a roll, Dave rolls, Alice /reloads (sessions are memory-only), opens /cdl drops and clicks Roll again for the same item. A probe run of the same steps showed what follows. Bob's roll popup still points at the old session. Bob's roll went into the new session on Alice and into the old one on everyone else. After the award, every other client still had new=cancelled / old=closed, Bob's popup read 'You rolled 60 - rolls closed' (never 'You won'), and the council panels showed no winner. Code: in OnRollStart (Roll.lua:1194-1204), OtherOpen finds the stale old session (still open for up to endsAt+3 s). Earlier(other, ses) is true, so the new session is set to 'cancelled'. OnRollWin (Roll.lua:1277) drops RW for cancelled sessions, and OnRollEnd ignores it too.
rootCause: The simultaneous-start rule always prefers the earlier session. It does not notice that the 'earlier' open session belongs to the same starter, who evidently lost it (reload, crash, relog) and has started a new one.
proposedFix: In OnRollStart, before the Earlier() comparison: if other.starter == sender (the same player now starts another roll), treat the old session as stale. CancelSession(other) or CloseSession(other), then accept the new RS. Optionally also accept RW for a 'cancelled' session when its sender is the session's starter.

title: Handing the item out before confirming flips the roll suggestion away from the winner (and the announce tier word becomes 'roll')
evidence: test_award.py::handed_out_before_confirming_keeps_bis_winner FAILS. Bob (BiS main) rolls 54, Dave (alt) 80, Frank (not listed) 99, and the roll closes with Bob suggested. The ML then gives the item to Bob from the normal master-loot menu (GiveMasterLoot(1,2)). The failure reads "after the item was handed to Bob the suggestion moved to 'Dave-Thunderstrike': [... Dave tier 2 suggested ..., Bob tier 3]". So the panel's primary button becomes 'Award to Dave'. TierOf (Roll.lua:578-586) demotes a player to tier 3 when w.obtained, or when w.awarded and key ~= ses.winner. The loot-message auto ledger entry for this very item makes HasAward true within 0.2 s, and Bob's bag scan plus list sync (about 10 s later) makes obtained true. Finish (Roll.lua:1039-1046) takes the tier word from the same live BuildResults, so the confirmed award is announced as '(rolled 54, roll)' instead of 'BiS'.
rootCause: Results and tiers are recomputed live from the ledger and list data even after the roll closed. The effects of handing out this drop (the auto ledger entry, the winner's obtained flag) are treated as 'already has it'.
proposedFix: Snapshot each row's tier, which, phase and obtained values when the session closes (in CloseSession / OnRollEnd), and use the snapshot for GetResults, the suggestion and Finish afterwards. Alternatively, ignore ledger entries and obtained changes for ses.i that are newer than ses.startedAt when computing TierOf.

title: Two council members awarding the same roll at nearly the same time leave clients disagreeing on the winner and credit the item twice
evidence: test_award.py::simultaneous_awards_by_two_council_members_agree FAILS: "clients disagree on the winner: {'Alice': 'Dave-Thunderstrike', 'Bob': 'Bob-Thunderstrike', 'Carol': 'Dave-Thunderstrike', ...}". Alice confirms Bob and Bob confirms Dave in the same moment, through CDLOOT_CONFIRM_AWARD on both. OnRollWin (Roll.lua:1274-1289) accepts RW for a session that is already 'awarded' and overwrites winner unconditionally, so the last message wins on each client. Each Finish (Roll.lua:1070-1073) also writes its own manual ledger entry with a different winner, so both stay visible in the award log.
rootCause: There is no deterministic rule for conflicting RW messages, and a losing local award is never rolled back.
proposedFix: Send the award server time (and awarder) in RW. In OnRollWin, when ses.state == 'awarded' and the winner differs, keep the earliest award (tie: smaller awarder key) on every client. The client whose award lost voids its own ledger entry (keep the entry id on the session; call Ledger:Void) and prints a conflict warning.

title: Fallback drop source key uses the per-machine GetTime(), so a second looter of the same corpse creates a duplicate drop
evidence: test_drops.py::loot_source_nil_second_looter_no_duplicate FAILS when GetLootSourceInfo returns nil (shimmed on all clients). The ML opens the corpse, and 1 s later Bob (council) opens the same corpse. Result: "second D ['UNKNOWN-424'], drops per client {'Alice': ['UNKNOWN-419', 'UNKNOWN-424'], 'Bob': [...both...], ...}": every client gets two DROP events and two history pages for one corpse. Loot.lua:280 builds guid = "UNKNOWN-" .. floor(GetTime() / 30). GetTime() has a different base on every machine, so the keys differ across clients, and the dedupe by source key (IsSeen / remoteSeen) cannot match them. Even on one client, a 30 s bucket boundary splits the key. The companion case loot_source_nil_uses_recent_boss passes, so the single-looter fallback works.
rootCause: The fallback source identity depends on a client-local clock and never matches between clients.
proposedFix: Use a key every client computes the same way. One option is "UNKNOWN-" .. (GetRecentBossKey() or "") .. "-" .. floor(GetServerTime()/120). Also add a receive-side dedupe for UNKNOWN-* drops: ignore a D whose sorted item list equals a drop seen in the last ~2 minutes.

title: Sunmote upgrade (and arena exchange) matches are labelled 'via token' in the toast, the BiS chat line and the roll popup
evidence: test_drops.py::sunmote_upgrade_base_drop_alerts_upgrade_wanters FAILS: "Sunmote upgrade described as a token: '|cffa336edRobes of Ghostly Hatred|r - Chest · P5 (main, via token)'". test_drops.py::sunmote_upgrade_roll_popup_text FAILS: "roll popup calls the Sunmote upgrade a token: '* Your P5 BiS (main) - Chest (via token)'". The drop was Robes of Faltered Light 34233 from M'uru, and Dave has 34399 on his P5 BiS. BiS:MatchItem returns via='upgrade', but DropPanel.lua:661 (PrintOwnDrop), DropPanel.lua:2013 (RefreshToastText) and RollFrame.lua:178 (OwnStatusText) all print ', via token' / '(via token)' for any m.via. Tooltip.lua:24 already maps via correctly (VIA_TEXT = {token=..., upgrade='via Sunmote upgrade', arena='via token exchange'}).
rootCause: The via kind is ignored in three text builders; they assume every indirect match is a tier token.
proposedFix: Share Tooltip's VIA_TEXT mapping (for example as ns.VIA_TEXT in Constants) and use VIA_TEXT[m.via] in DropPanel.lua:661, DropPanel.lua:2013 and RollFrame.lua:178.

title: A non-council master looter / raid lead gets a suggestion that ignores BiS priority (everyone is tier 3 on their client)
evidence: test_award.py::non_council_master_looter_suggestion_follows_bis_tiers FAILS: "the master looter's panel suggests ['Zed-Thunderstrike'], the council's ['Bob-Thunderstrike']". Setup: Frank is ML (guild rank 2, not council), Bob (BiS main) rolls 10, Zed (not listed) rolls 90. Roll:CanStart and CanAward (Roll.lua:757-767) allow a non-council ML or lead to start and award, and DropPanel shows 'Award to <suggested>' as the primary button (DropPanel.lua:1580-1588). BuildResults (Roll.lua:627) takes tiers from Store:GetWanters, but on a non-council client Store:GetAllKeys (Store.lua:151-168) contains only the player's own list. So every other roller is tier 3 and the highest roll wins.
rootCause: The suggestion needs everyone's lists, which only council clients hold; nothing tells a non-council awarder that their suggestion ignores BiS.
proposedFix: Two options. (a) Council clients broadcast their suggestion or tiers for a session (for example in an extra field of RE or a small RT message), and non-council awarders display those. (b) At minimum, when not AmICouncil(true), hide the 'Suggested' tag and the 'Award to <suggested>' primary button and show 'BiS priority unknown - ask the loot council'.

title: Roll awards confirmed by a non-council ML / raid lead are never written to the award log (lost entirely for trade hand-outs)
evidence: test_award.py::non_council_master_looter_award_reaches_the_award_log FAILS: "Alice: roll award by the (non-council) ML missing from the log: []". Frank (non-council ML) runs a roll, closes the loot window, and awards Bob through CDLOOT_CONFIRM_AWARD (a trade hand-out, so no loot message). Every client shows the session awarded to Bob via RW, but no council client has a ledger entry. Finish writes the ledger only when ses.demo or AmRealCouncil() (Roll.lua:1070-1073), and OnRollWin (Roll.lua:1274-1289) on council clients never records. Spec Addendum §19.1 step 3 requires Ledger:Award for every roll award, while §11 makes the ledger council-only.
rootCause: The award record is written only by the awarding client, which cannot write the ledger when it is not council, and no council client picks up the award from RW.
proposedFix: When a real-council client receives RW (or awards itself), record Ledger:Award with an id derived from the session id (for example 'm'..sessionID). Every council client then creates the same id and the entries merge instead of duplicating. The later loot-message auto entry is hidden by the existing manual-wins rule.

title: The roll suggestion can pick a player who already left the raid
evidence: test_rolls.py::departed_roller_not_suggested FAILS: "suggested ['Frank-Thunderstrike'] although Frank left the raid: [{'suggested': True, 'inRaid': False, ..., 'roll': 97}, {... 'Dave' ..., 'roll': 30}]". Frank rolls 97, Dave rolls 30, then Frank leaves the group before the roll closes. BuildResults (Roll.lua:667-690) keeps every recorded roll in group 1 (RowGroup, Roll.lua:604-608) and suggests out[1] regardless of r.inRaid. The master-loot give to a departed player then fails ('not eligible', fallback confirm popup; see ml_award_to_player_not_eligible_falls_back_to_confirm, which passes).
rootCause: inRaid is computed per row but not used when ordering or suggesting.
proposedFix: Treat valid rolls of players no longer in the group as a lower group: return 2 from RowGroup when not Util.IsInMyGroup(r.key). The row stays visible but is never 'suggested'.

title: A real roll that is still closed but not awarded can be awarded after demo mode is turned on; the award is announced to the raid but never saved to the real loot log or sent to other raiders
evidence: Harness test tests/conformance/test_demo_isolation.py, scenario C. Alice (council) starts a real roll in a raid, Bob /rolls 77, Alice ends the roll, then turns on /cdl demo, awards the session to Bob and accepts CDLOOT_CONFIRM_AWARD. Results: CDLootDB.ledger holds 0 entries while the demo view holds 1; Bob's session stays in state 'closed' because no RW arrives; after /cdl demo off the real ledger is still 0, so the award is lost. How the code gets there: Roll.lua:1297-1317 OnDemoToggled cancels only sessions in state 'open' or 'queued', so closed real sessions can still be awarded. Roll.lua:764-767 CanAward returns true whenever demo is on. Finish (Roll.lua:1071-1076) chooses isolation by the session: it calls Ledger:Award whenever `ses.demo or AmRealCouncil()` and sends RW whenever `not ses.demo`. The callees, however, check the global demo flag. Ledger:Award (Ledger.lua:327-352, via ActiveDB at 55-58) writes into the in-memory demoEntries while DemoOn(), and OnDemoToggled (Ledger.lua:598-604) throws that table away. Roll's Send (Roll.lua:115-116) returns false while DemoOn(), so RW is never sent. Meanwhile Announce(body, not AnnounceOn()) at Roll.lua:1081-1082 still posts the winner line to the real raid chat. The same happens on the CDLOOT_GIVE_ITEM path: the item really is handed out with GiveMasterLoot, but no manual ledger entry and no RW follow.
rootCause: Roll decides isolation per session (ses.demo), while Ledger and Roll's own Send decide by the global Demo:IsEnabled(). A session created before demo was switched on falls between the two.
proposedFix: Choose one rule. Option 1: in Roll's OnDemoToggled, also cancel or freeze non-demo sessions in state 'closed', and make Roll:Award / CanAward refuse `not ses.demo` sessions while DemoOn(). Option 2: give Ledger an explicit real-write path (for example Ledger:Award(..., {real=true})), have Finish use it for non-demo sessions, and let Roll's Send skip only when ses.demo is set.

title: Loot's D handler rechecks the sender with the demo-aware Util.IsInMyGroup, so real raid drops are dropped while demo mode is on
evidence: Harness test tests/conformance/test_demo_isolation.py, scenario A. Bob is master looter and opens a boss corpse, which sends a D on CDLa/RAID. Control run with demo off: Alice's dropHistory goes 0 -> 1. Run with Alice in demo mode: dropHistory stays 0 -> 0 although Bob's D was sent, so no council panel and no personal toast. Code: Loot.lua:238-244 OnDropMessage runs `if not Util.IsInMyGroup(sender) then return end` before `remoteSeen[s] = true`. Util.lua:490-496 IsInMyGroup returns `ns.Demo:IsInDemoRaid(key)` when demo is on, and that is only true for fake members and me. Comm.lua:72-81 and 281-282 has already accepted the message using IsRealGroupMember (the real Util.group or UnitInRaid), which is the SPEC §10.1 gate. Because remoteSeen is never set, Alice's own pending D broadcast for the same source is not suppressed either.
rootCause: The handler adds a second group gate that uses demo semantics. The transport layer already applied the real group gate required by the spec.
proposedFix: Remove the redundant check at Loot.lua:241, or replace it with a real-group check (for example `Util.group[sender]`, the same IsRealGroupMember logic Comm uses). Distribution is already restricted to RAID/PARTY at line 240.

title: Demo mode posts fake demo member names to real raid or party chat through the drop panel and Council 'Announce' actions
evidence: Harness probe tests/conformance/probe_announce.py and scenario B of test_demo_isolation.py: Alice is in a real raid with demo on and calls DropPanel:AnnounceItem(28822). world.chat_log records the RAID line 'CDLoot: [Teeth of Gruul] - BiS: Aldrin; Alt: Isolde'; Aldrin and Isolde are Demo fake names. Code: DropPanel.lua:1707-1726 BuildAnnounceLine takes names from Store:GetWanters, which returns demo records when demo is on (Store.lua:39-46, 142-148), and filters on w.inRaid from the demo raid. AnnounceItem (DropPanel.lua:1729-1741) only keeps `test` drops local and otherwise calls ns.UI:AnnounceLine, which sends to RAID/PARTY chat (Widgets.lua:1010-1031). AnnounceAll (1745-1762) follows the same path. Council.lua:1041-1067 announceItem (Items view, 'Announce to raid') has no demo guard either. Compare Roll.lua:522-523 and 1079-1080, which print demo lines locally as ADDENDUM A §19.2 requires, and §20: 'Make sure no other demo data leaks into SavedVariables or comms'.
rootCause: The announce paths only check `drop.test`, not Demo:IsEnabled(). While demo is on the wanter data is fake, but the chat channel is real.
proposedFix: In DropPanel:AnnounceItem, treat `DemoEnabled()` like `test` (print locally with a '[demo, not sent]' prefix). Add the same guard to Council.lua announceItem, or centralise it in UI:AnnounceLine with an explicit allowDemo flag.

title: UI:ItemText returns (text, loadingFlag); two call sites pass both into GameTooltip:AddLine, so the boolean lands in the r (red) colour argument
evidence: Widgets.lua:245-251: `return "|cff808080Loading...|r", true` / `return "|c"..Hex(...)..name.."|r", false`. The local wrappers `itemText` (Council.lua:144-150 and LootLog.lua:69-75) forward both values (`return ns.UI:ItemText(itemID)`). Council.lua:1110 calls `GameTooltip:AddLine(itemText(d.itemID))` and LootLog.lua:263 calls `GameTooltip:AddLine(itemText(tonumber(e.i)))`, which becomes AddLine(text, false|true), so a boolean is the red channel. The other sites in the same files wrap the call in parentheses (`(itemText(id))`, Council.lua:191 and 721). DropPanel.lua:113, RollFrame.lua:103 and Tooltip.lua:81 also drop the second value on purpose ('drop the extra "loading" return value'). The mock's AddLine does not type-check (tools/wowmock/ui.lua:616), so the harness cannot show the effect. On the real client, at best the header line gets a wrong colour; at worst a strict argument check rejects the boolean.
rootCause: UI:ItemText returns a second value, and these two call sites were not adjusted, unlike the other callers.
proposedFix: Wrap the calls: `GameTooltip:AddLine((itemText(d.itemID)))` and `GameTooltip:AddLine((itemText(tonumber(e.i))))`. Better, make both local itemText wrappers return only the first value (`local t = ns.UI:ItemText(id); return t`).

title: Guild config tag is read and written through deprecation-only aliases GetGuildInfoText / SetGuildInfoText
evidence: CDLoot reads the guild info text with `GetGuildInfoText and GetGuildInfoText()` (Core/Guild.lua:213, :470). It writes it with `SetGuildInfoText(text)` (Core/Guild.lua:483), and WriteConfig refuses to run when `not SetGuildInfoText` (Core/Guild.lua:459). On this client these globals exist only as deprecation fallbacks. The classic_anniversary branch head is commit 1463c68627 '2.5.6 (69795)', which is the installed build (C:\World of Warcraft\.build.info: 2.5.6.69795). In that source, Interface/AddOns/Blizzard_DeprecatedGuildScript/Deprecated_GuildScript.lua starts with `if not GetCVarBool("loadDeprecationFallbacks") then return; end` and later has `-- Deprecated in 12.0.1 onwards. GetGuildInfoText = C_GuildInfo.GetInfoText; SetGuildInfoText = C_GuildInfo.SetInfoText;`. This was added in 2.5.6 (68502), commit fa643dda0b, the same commit that added C_GuildInfo.GetInfoText and SetInfoText to Blizzard_APIDocumentationGenerated/GuildInfoDocumentation.lua:103/:300. Blizzard's own TBC guild UI calls only the new API: Blizzard_UIPanels_Game/Classic/FriendsFrame.xml:3389 `local guildInfoText = C_GuildInfo.GetInfoText();` and :3433 `C_GuildInfo.SetInfoText(GuildInfoEditBox:GetText());`. CanEditGuildInfo() stays a native global and is correct (FriendsFrame.xml:3347). No installed 20506 addon reads GetGuildInfoText (tools/known_globals count 0). https://github.com/Gethe/wow-ui-source/blob/classic_anniversary/Interface/AddOns/Blizzard_DeprecatedGuildScript/Deprecated_GuildScript.lua
rootCause: The code was written against the pre-68502 global API. Since 2.5.6 build 68502 those globals are only aliases, loaded when the CVar loadDeprecationFallbacks is on. Blizzard says the aliases will be removed. If the CVar is off, or once the aliases are removed, several things fail silently. Every client parses an empty info text, so the CDL{...} council rank/add/remove and guild phase fall back to defaults once the cached-config grace period ends. For the GM or an officer, 'Save to Guild Information' prints the misleading 'You don't have permission to edit the Guild Information text.'
proposedFix: Define `local GetInfoText = (C_GuildInfo and C_GuildInfo.GetInfoText) or GetGuildInfoText` and `local SetInfoText = (C_GuildInfo and C_GuildInfo.SetInfoText) or SetGuildInfoText` at the top of Core/Guild.lua. Use them at :213, :459, :470 and :483, and keep CanEditGuildInfo() as it is. Add C_GuildInfo.GetInfoText and C_GuildInfo.SetInfoText to tools/wowmock/game.lua so the harness exercises the new path.

title: Spec auto-detect uses deprecation-only alias GetTalentTabInfo
evidence: BiS:DetectSpec returns "" when `not GetTalentTabInfo` (Core/BiS.lua:413) and otherwise calls `GetTalentTabInfo(tab)` (:417). On 2.5.6, GetTalentTabInfo is defined only in Blizzard_DeprecatedSpecialization/Deprecated_Specialization_TBC.lua:10. That file is gated by `if not GetCVarBool("loadDeprecationFallbacks") then return end` and is loaded through Deprecated_Specialization_[Game].lua in Blizzard_DeprecatedSpecialization.toc since 2.5.5 (65340). The alias wraps `C_SpecializationInfo.GetSpecializationInfo(specializationIndex, isInspect, isPet, inspectTarget, sex, groupIndex)`, which returns specId, name, description, icon, role, primaryStat, pointsSpent (7th), background, previewPointsSpent, isUnlocked (SpecializationInfoDocumentation.lua:76-101). Blizzard's TBC talent UI uses the native call: Blizzard_TalentUI/Classic/Blizzard_TalentUI.lua:524 `local _, name, _, icon, _, _, pointsSpent, background, previewPointsSpent = C_SpecializationInfo.GetSpecializationInfo(i, ...)`. GetNumTalentTabs, which CDLoot also uses, is native (Blizzard_TalentUI.lua:515).
rootCause: The addon relies on the backwards-compatibility alias instead of the native C_SpecializationInfo API. When fallbacks are not loaded, the spec label is never auto-detected, and nothing reports it.
proposedFix: In DetectSpec, read the points as `select(7, C_SpecializationInfo.GetSpecializationInfo(tab, false, false, nil, nil, nil))` when C_SpecializationInfo and C_SpecializationInfo.GetSpecializationInfo exist. Keep the current GetTalentTabInfo branch as a fallback, since both give pointsSpent at the same position after remapping. Add C_SpecializationInfo.GetSpecializationInfo to the mock.

title: The '→' (U+2192) glyph is missing from FRIZQT__.TTF
evidence: `local body = strformat("%s → %s (%s, %s)", ItemText(ses), Util.ShortName(key), rollText, ...)` (Core/Roll.lua:1077). Group chat gets a gsub to '->' (:167). The local/demo path shows the raw body through ns:Print, and the award result is shown there whenever announcements are off (:1080/:1082). I decoded the character map of the client's own Friz Quadrata TT (cached as C:\World of Warcraft\_anniversary_\Fonts\615960.slug) with scratchpad\tests\client-api\slug_cmap.py. The decoder checks out against known glyphs: all of Latin-1, the cp1252 extras (€ ™ – — … •) and the MacRoman extras (ı ƒ ∂ ∞ ◊) are present, Hangul and CJK are absent. Result: U+2192 → has NO glyph in FRIZQT__ or FRIZQT___CYR (it exists only in the Korean/Chinese fallback fonts). U+25BE ▾, U+2605 ★ and U+2713/2714 ✓✔ are also missing. Present: U+00B7 ·, U+00D7 ×, U+2014 —, U+2026 …, U+2022 •. The chat frame font is ChatFontNormal, which inherits NumberFont_Shadow_Med with roman member Fonts\ARIALN.TTF (Blizzard_Fonts_Shared/Classic/Fonts.xml:265-267). ARIALN is not in the local font cache, so whether it has the arrow cannot be checked here. It will show as a gap for anyone whose chat or UI font is Friz-based.
rootCause: The format string itself uses a non-cp1252 glyph. Only the group-chat path replaces it.
proposedFix: Put '->' directly into the format string at Core/Roll.lua:1077, then drop the gsub at :167 (or keep it as a guard). No other raw glyph in code needs changing. ★ and ✓ are already emitted as |T textures, and the remaining non-ASCII characters (· × — …) are present in FRIZQT__.
